standard.title: Create using literary elements
standard.description: create and edit imaginative texts, using or adapting language features, characters, events and settings that reflect their own world
standard.prior_knowledge: Students create and edit literary texts by adapting structures and language features of familiar texts (AC9E2LE05). They have not yet focused on using or adapting characters, events and settings that reflect their own world as a source for original imaginative text creation.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create and edit imaginative texts using or adapting language features, characters, events and settings that reflect their own world.

nodes.label: Drawing on literary texts for inspiration
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can draw on literary texts they have read for inspiration and ideas, adapting settings or changing endings to create their own texts.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a short imaginative text that adapts at least one element (setting, character type, event or ending) from a read text, explaining what was borrowed and what was changed.
nodes.typical_width: Draw on literary texts for inspiration — adapting texts by changing setting or revising an ending; creating texts that reflect their own world through character, event or setting choices.
wider: Adapt a traditional story by shifting the setting to a familiar Australian or local context, and discuss how the story changes as a result
Create a text that uses a character type from a read text but places them in a situation from the student's own experience, discussing how the known character behaves in the new context

response_modes.reason: Creative text creation at Y3 is supported by having a repertoire of literary elements to draw from. Students who have encountered a range of character types, settings and event structures across their reading have more resources to adapt. This is a strand where reading breadth directly enables writing.

success_criteria: Student creates an imaginative text that draws identifiably on at least one element from a known literary text
Student can explain what was adapted and what reflects their own ideas or world

nodes.label: Using language features from literature in own writing
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use language features from literary texts they have studied (e.g. descriptive language, dialogue, imagery) in their own imaginative writing.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least one language feature from a studied text (e.g. imagery, a specific type of descriptive language, dialogue) in an original imaginative text.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss characters encountered in literary texts and how those characters might behave in new situations; create imaginative texts using language features from studied texts including descriptive language, dialogue, imagery and characterisation techniques.
wider: Use literary devices discussed in LE04 (imagery, sound devices) deliberately in a creative text, and explain why each device was chosen
Compare a first draft with a revised version where a language feature has been deliberately improved — discussing what the revision achieves

response_modes.reason: Using literary language features in original writing requires students to integrate their knowledge of what devices do (from analysis) with creative composition decisions (when and where to use them). The bridge from reader to writer is the integration challenge at this node.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Creative writing that consciously applies literary language features is motivating and developmentally significant for Y3. Students become authors rather than just readers of these techniques. The connection between analysis (LE03, LE04) and creation (LE05) is genuinely enriching territory.
success_criteria: Student uses at least one identified language feature (naming it) in their own text
Student can explain why they chose that feature at that point in their writing
